OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized into E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped;
            a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise the
            '+61' country code is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from
            the national digits. The result must be a '+' followed by 8 to 15
            digits, e.g. '0412 345 678' is stored as '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be a
            syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string

## Summary

I implemented the household-duplicate rule for owner creation. When a request would create an owner whose **lastName and address both match an existing owner** (compared case-insensitively, with leading/trailing whitespace trimmed and internal runs of whitespace collapsed to a single space), it's now rejected with **409 Conflict** — unless the request sets **`sharesHousehold: true`**, which opts in and allows the create.

Changes, following the existing `DuplicateTelephoneException` pattern in the codebase:

- **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — added a write-only `sharesHousehold` boolean to the `OwnerFields` schema so the generated `OwnerFieldsDto` exposes `getSharesHousehold()`.
- **`rest/advice/DuplicateHouseholdException.java`** (new) — thrown when the rule is violated.
- **`rest/advice/ExceptionControllerAdvice.java`** — added a handler translating it to 409 with `errors: ["lastName", "address"]`.
- **`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — added a `collapse(...)` normalizer and a `rejectDuplicateHousehold(...)` guard invoked at the start of `addOwner`, skipped when `sharesHousehold` is true.

Test results: `Cp10Tests` (the household-duplicate checkpoint) passes all 3 cases — reject on same lastName+address, allow with different address, allow with `sharesHousehold: true` — and the full suite (20 tests across Cp01–Cp10) is green with no regressions.
